El fondo de maniobra, $FM = AC − PC$, es: Working capital, $WC = CA − CL$, is the part of current assets financed in the long term. If it is negative, the company cannot pay its short-term debts with what it has in the short term.
Los ratios de liquidez comparan el activ: Liquidity ratios compare current assets with short-term debts (current ratio, between 1.5 and 2; quick ratio, excluding inventories, between 0.75 and 1; cash ratio, with cash only, between 0.1 and 0.3). The solvency ratio compares all assets with all debts (between 1.5 and 2.5). The recommended values are indicative: they depend a lot on the sector.
El endeudamiento, la parte del activo fi: The debt ratio, the part of assets financed with debt, should be between 0.4 and 0.6. Autonomy compares equity with debts, and debt quality says what part falls due in the short term: the lower, the better.
La rentabilidad económica, $ROA = BAII/A: Return on assets, $ROA = EBIT/TA$, measures what the assets yield; it is margin times turnover. Return on equity, $ROE = {"net income"}/{E}$, what the owners' money yields. If debt costs less than the assets yield ($i < ROA$), borrowing raises the ROE: this is financial leverage, $ROE = [ROA + (ROA − i) L/E](1 − t)$.
